title: Surgical Win
reviewNotes: Four branches, 16 exact positions from the complete six-piece source board. Winning king route Kb3-c2-d1 avoids pawn-check tempos before f5. Compared drawing immediate f5, Kb4 c5+ Kc3, and Kb3 c5 Kc3 Kc6. Selected winning line ends after Kc2 blocks the pawn on c3; no invented continuation of the later race.

If you play f5, this is actually a mistake. We are trying to create a passed pawn, but after black takes, we are actually not in time to promote because black is going to get a queen of his own. But if we want to move the king closer with the idea that we're going to stop the black pawn and then get our queen, this is actually still a mistake. [music] After c5, black gains one precious tempo on this king. After the king moves, we still cannot go f5. Black takes and despite being able to stop the black pawn, black is going to have another pawn running to promotion and we cannot stop both of these pawns at the same time. One of the two is going to become a queen and this is another draw. So going back to the beginning, the only winning move is the very precise king to >> [music] >> b3. Now still trying to approach the black pawn, but avoiding any checks from this other pawn. Black of course still pushes trying to get another queen. Now of course we don't want to rush with f5, but also if we go to c3, this is still another mistake. After a move like king to c6 just waiting around, black has the upper hand. We cannot go f5. After black takes, we can't stop the pawn, but we have to step on a dark square which is going to put us in a position where black is going [music] to be able at the right time to give us a check with the pawn. If we take this pawn, black is going to get a queen, but if we go to the other pawn, now black is going to promote this one and again this is a draw. So the only path to victory is to continue marching down the light square with king to c2. Black is going to push again and now that we understand the mechanics of this position, we can come to the conclusion that the only winning move here is king to D1. And now black has no drawing mechanism anymore. If the king tries to get closer, we can now sacrifice the F pawn and the black pawns are simply not fast enough to get a queen on their own. >> [music] >> White is going to be able to stop them and win the game. But if black insists in not moving the black king and wasting any tempo and plays pawn to C3, now we still sacrifice the F pawn and finally the last nail [music] in this coffin is king to C2. We prevent the advance of the C pawn. So black has to either push the other pawn or run with the king. But this time, almost magically, our king is going to be able to stop both of the pawns. The king is too far to stop our pawn and we are well close enough to stop the black pawn. So white is going to get a queen and finally win this incredible end game.
